newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-LARA WORLD RECORD IN JAYASURIYA'S SIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA WORLD RECORD IN JAYASURIYA'S SIGHTS.

text.p: Sri Lanka opener Sanath Jayasuriya completed only the 14th triple century in test history on Tuesday and left himself on the verge of beating Brian Lara's individual test record score of 375.
Jayasuriya, who began the fourth day against India on 175, was 326 not out at the close, just 50 short of breaking the mark set by Lara for the West Indies against England in Antigua three years ago.

The left-handed Jayasuriya has already claimed the highest score made by a Sri Lankan and his unbroken second wicket partnership of 548 with Roshan Mahanama, unbeaten on 211, was also a record for any wicket in test cricket.

They also became only the second pair to bat through two entire days of a test, the only other occasion being Gary Sobers and Frank Worrell for the West Indies against England at Bridgetown in 1959-60.
"It was a fantastic effort by both batsmen and I hope Roshan will also end up with a triple century," said Sri Lanka coach Duleep Mendis.
"They have the confidence now and although they are physically and mentally tired, they are still going on with 100 percent concentration.
"The situation doesn't demand a declaration and it is the ideal opportunity for both of them to achieve their personal goals."
With one day remaining, and Sri Lanka on 587 for one and leading India by 50, a draw looks certain.

After wiping out Don Bradman and Bill Ponsford's second wicket record of 451 for Australia against England in 1934, they went on to beat the previous best for any wicket of 467 scored by New Zealanders Andrew Jones and Martin Crowe against Sri Lanka in Wellington in 1991.
The two batsmen are only 29 runs short of equalling the record partnership in all first-class cricket of 577 set by V.S. Hazare and Gul Mahomed for Baroda against Holkar in 1946-47.
Jayasuriya became the highest individual scorer for Sri Lanka when he passed the 267 which Aravinda de Silva made in the same test that Jones and Crowe set their record.
"I knew I had broken Aravinda's record and at that stage I wanted to make 300," he said.

He reached that landmark by on-driving left-arm spinner Nilesh Kulkarni to long-on for his 32nd four. It took him 723 minutes and 518 balls and included one six. His 326 is already the eighth highest score in test history.
"Tomorrow I will not think of any records but play according to the balls I receive," he added.
Mahanama playing solidly, surpassed his previous highest test score of 153 and by the close he had moved on to 211. He faced 551 balls in 740 minutes and hit 25 fours.
"Records are there to fall and I think we have a good chance of breaking them," he said.
